arguments.question: For each portfolio, show the total value of Technology sector holdings and what percentage it represents of the total portfolio value
arguments.sql:
WITH PortfolioValues AS (
    SELECT 
        h.portfolio_id,
        SUM(h.quantity * s.current_price) AS total_portfolio_value
    FROM holdings h
    JOIN securities s ON h.security_id = s.security_id
    GROUP BY h.portfolio_id
),
TechValues AS (
    SELECT 
        h.portfolio_id,
        SUM(h.quantity * s.current_price) AS tech_value
    FROM holdings h
    JOIN securities s ON h.security_id = s.security_id
    JOIN sectors sec ON s.sector_id = sec.sector_id
    WHERE sec.sector_name = 'Technology'
    GROUP BY h.portfolio_id
)
SELECT 
    p.portfolio_name,
    tv.tech_value,
    pv.total_portfolio_value,
    ROUND((tv.tech_value / pv.total_portfolio_value) * 100, 2) AS tech_percentage
FROM TechValues tv
JOIN PortfolioValues pv ON tv.portfolio_id = pv.portfolio_id
JOIN portfolios p ON tv.portfolio_id = p.portfolio_id
ORDER BY tech_percentage DESC;

arguments.sql:
SELECT 
    p.portfolio_name, 
    COUNT(DISTINCT s.sector_id) AS sector_count, 
    COUNT(h.holding_id) AS total_holdings,
    ROUND(CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT s.sector_id) AS REAL) / COUNT(h.holding_id), 3) AS diversification_ratio
FROM portfolios p
JOIN holdings h ON p.portfolio_id = h.portfolio_id
JOIN securities s ON h.security_id = s.security_id
GROUP BY p.portfolio_id
HAVING sector_count > 5
ORDER BY diversification_ratio DESC;
arguments.explanation: To find portfolios with holdings in more than 5 different sectors, I join portfolios, holdings, and securities (which links to sectors). I group by portfolio_name, count the distinct sectors and total holdings, and calculate the diversification ratio (sector_count / total_holdings). I filter for sector_count > 5 and order by the diversification ratio descending.
